title: Failover: dashboards for region health + state transitions; add multi-window burn-rate alerts for multi-region SLO
author: Sergio Costa
body: Summary: Add first-pass dashboards and alert rules for the Regional failover automation upgrade. This PR introduces (1) a Region Health Overview dashboard, (2) a Failover State Machine / Transition Audit dashboard, (3) a Customer Impact dashboard split by customer tier + route/model scope, and (4) multi-window burn-rate alerts mapped to the multi-region availability SLO. Motivation: During recent regional degradations we had the data, but not a single place to see (a) which health signals were driving a failover recommendation/decision, (b) whether we were flapping on thresholds, and (c) the customer-visible impact by tier/route while mitigation was in progress. These dashboards are intended to be the default landing page for on-call during failover decisions and to support controlled failover game days. What’s included: Dashboards: Region Health Overview (by region): request volume, 5xx rate, 4xx rate, p50/p95/p99 latency, upstream dependency health summary, queue depth saturation, GPU headroom, synthetic probe status, and network path loss/RTT signals; Failover Orchestrator State: current mode (normal/monitor-only/degraded/failing-over/failed-over), last transition, transition reason (signal + threshold), hold-down timer remaining, manual override status, and a compact timeline of state transitions; Customer Impact: error rate and tail latency sliced by customer tier (hosted vs dedicated), and by route/model scope when present in routing policy labels. Alerting: Add burn-rate alerts (fast/slow) for multi-region availability SLO and multi-region tail latency SLO, plus failover-specific alerts for trigger engine evaluation anomalies (no signal updates, inconsistent region health, stuck state transitions, excessive transition rate indicating flapping). Burn-rate alerts are explicitly designed to page only when error budget burn suggests meaningful customer impact; failover-signal alerts are ticket/Slack by default unless we’re in an active failover state. Implementation notes: - Uses existing SLO recording rules but adds a dedicated multi-region SLO group so the dashboards can link directly to SLO budget remaining and recent burn history. - Adds a shared PromQL library for region labels and tier scoping to reduce copy/paste across panels. - Adds explicit "monitor_only" and "manual_override" annotations to avoid paging confusion during game days and controlled tests. Rollout plan: - Land dashboards + alerts in staging first; verify label availability for hosted + dedicated traffic. - Enable burn-rate paging for hosted (tier=hosted) first; dedicated paging remains notify-only until we validate with Harish’s capacity signals and dedicated SLO baselines. - During game day, we’ll pin the dashboards in #incidents and use the Failover Orchestrator State dashboard as the primary “what is happening” view. Screenshots: (internal) linked in Linear ENG-2847 comment 12. Testing: PromQL validated against staging + prod read-only queries; dashboard jsonnet compiled via CI; alerts validated via promtool. Follow-ups (not in scope): - Correlation links from transition timeline to incident-bot messages (owned by ENG-2848). - Add per-model fallback effectiveness panels once fallback metrics are finalized in redwood PR 98322.
commits: dashboards: add region health overview (core signals + synthetic probes)
dashboards: add failover state machine + transition timeline panels
dashboards: add customer impact by tier/route/model scoping
alerts: add MWMB burn-rate alerts for multi-region SLOs
alerts: add failover flapping + stuck-transition detectors with monitor-only annotations
chore: refactor shared promql helpers + panel templates; run jsonnetfmt
conversation: Allison Grant (review): Panels look good overall. Two concerns: (1) We need a single canonical label mapping for region (we’ve had region vs pop vs cluster in the past). (2) The burn-rate alerts should not page on missing-data artifacts during partial metric pipeline impairment. Can we harden with absent()/for windows and add annotations for monitor-only? Sergio Costa (author): Agree on both. I switched all panels/alerts to use the lib/promql/regions helper (region_id) and removed direct usage of cluster where possible. For missing-data, I added an explicit "signal_stale" alert (notify-only) and gated paging burn-rate expressions to require request volume > 0 and to ignore series with absent data. Also added a runbook link + monitor_only annotation plumbed from the failover orchestrator labels. Aisha Bello (review): Thanks. For burn-rate, can we match the multi-window multi-burn guidance from the SLO policy (fast: 2%/1h + 5%/6h; slow: 2%/6h + 10%/3d). Also, please ensure latency SLO pages are separate from availability pages (we don’t want dual paging for the same incident). Sergio Costa (author): Updated to MWMB per policy and added inhibit rules so availability pages take precedence when both fire. Latency pages only when availability is OK. Felix Schneider (review): Dashboard UX: the transition timeline panel is helpful, but can you add a "last safe-to-failover gate result" stat and a link to the audit log explorer? Even if the underlying metric is a placeholder, the panel should exist so on-call knows where to look. Sergio Costa (author): Added panels for capacity/dependency gate results (using the current gate metrics names from redwood PR 98305) and a link-out to the audit log explorer. If the metric is missing, panel shows "No data" with a note pointing to staged rollout. Miles Thornton (review): One more: flapping detector threshold seems low (3 transitions/15m). We expect some churn during canary progressive failover and don’t want noise. Suggest increase to 6 transitions/15m and only alert when not in monitor-only. Sergio Costa (author): Updated flapping detector to 6/15m, and added condition `failover_monitor_only == 0` before firing. CI note: First run failed jsonnetfmt due to trailing commas in new templated panels; fixed and pushed. Allison Grant (final): Approved after latest changes. Please make sure README includes where to find the dashboards in Grafana and the default on-call view order. Sergio Costa (author): Done. Squashed and ready.
release_notes: Internal: Adds new Grafana dashboards (Failover/Region Health, Failover/State Transitions, Failover/Customer Impact) and burn-rate + failover-signal alerting rules aligned to the multi-region SLO policy; intended for staging first, then progressive prod enablement.
